title: From a grammar: S → aSb | ε
notes: Sipser's construction turns a grammar into a PDA: push S$, then in q1 either replace the variable on top by one of its right-hand sides (an ε-move) or match the terminal on top with the next input symbol. The stack holds what is still to be matched, and the accepting computation follows a leftmost derivation of the word.
ops: start q0; accept q2; q0 eps, eps -> q1 S$; q1 eps, S -> q1 aSb; q1 eps, S -> q1 eps; q1 a, a -> q1 eps; q1 b, b -> q1 eps; q1 eps, $ -> q2 eps
